chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abu Harun al-Makfuuf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
O Abu Harun, we command our children to recite the Tasbih of Fatimah (peace be upon her), just as we command them to pray. So adhere to it, for no servant recites it and becomes wretched.

key_terms.الْزَمْهُ: Adhere to it / Hold fast to it
key_terms.تَسْبِيحِ فَاطِمَةَ: The Tasbih of Fatimah, a specific collection of dhikr phrases attributed to Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her)
key_terms.فَشَقِيَ: And became wretched / failed to attain happiness

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Tasbih of Fatimah in Shia tradition and how is it practiced?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the Tasbih of Fatimah to the status of a fundamental household practice, instructing Abu Harun al-Makfuuf to teach it to children just as they are taught the daily prayers. This comparison underscores its role as a spiritual anchor for the family unit, with the Imam guaranteeing that consistent adherence leads to ultimate felicity (sa'adah), while neglect results in wretchedness (shaqa'ah).
